Tiny DSA is a Python reimplementation of the small Excel workbook described in
the [guidance note](../docs-source/guidance-note.md). It projects
general-government debt-to-GDP over five years from a baseline path and one
configurable stress scenario. The model is a transparent accounting exercise
for economists who want to trace the debt-dynamics identity, test assumptions,
or reproduce the corresponding Excel calculations. It is not an operational
debt-sustainability framework.

## The model in one equation

For each projection year, Tiny DSA applies

$$
D_t = D_{t-1}\frac{1+r_t}{1+g_t} - PB_t,
$$

where $D$ is debt-to-GDP, $r$ is the real interest rate, $g$ is real GDP
growth, and $PB$ is the primary balance. Rates and balances are entered as
percentage-point values (for example, `3.5`, not `0.035`). A positive primary
balance is a surplus and reduces debt.

::: {.callout-warning}
Tiny DSA is a methodological artifact, not an operational debt-sustainability
framework. It is not validated against country data and is not endorsed by the
IMF, the World Bank, or any other institution. Do not use its results for
policy decisions without a substantially richer model and independent review.
:::

## Interactive dependency graph

Each node is one bound series. Columns are **topological layers** (longest
path in the dependency DAG), so edges only run forward between columns — not
within a layer. Node colors mark input / internal / output. Click the diagram
to open the fullscreen interactive explorer (edit amber inputs, drag nodes,
Ctrl+Z undo).

```{=html}
<a
  class="tiny-dsa-graph-preview"
  id="tiny-dsa-graph-preview"
  href="assets/graph/index.html"
  target="_blank"
  rel="noopener"
  aria-label="Open the interactive Tiny DSA dependency graph"
>
  <iframe
    id="tiny-dsa-graph-frame"
    title="Tiny DSA dependency graph preview"
    loading="lazy"
    tabindex="-1"
    aria-hidden="true"
  ></iframe>
  <div class="tiny-dsa-graph-cta">
    <span>Open interactive graph</span>
    <span class="hint">Edit inputs · pan · zoom</span>
  </div>
</a>
<script>
(function () {
  var link = document.getElementById("tiny-dsa-graph-preview");
  var frame = document.getElementById("tiny-dsa-graph-frame");
  if (!link || !frame) return;
  // Great Docs publishes the app at site-root assets/graph/.
  var underGuide = /\/user-guide\//.test(location.pathname);
  var bases = underGuide
    ? ["../assets/graph/", "assets/graph/"]
    : ["assets/graph/", "../assets/graph/"];
  function apply(base) {
    link.href = new URL(base + "index.html", document.baseURI).href;
    frame.src = new URL(base + "index.html?preview=1", document.baseURI).href;
  }
  function tryNext(i) {
    if (i >= bases.length) {
      apply(bases[0]);
      return;
    }
    var probe = new URL(bases[i] + "index.html", document.baseURI).href;
    fetch(probe, { method: "GET", cache: "no-store" })
      .then(function (res) {
        if (res.ok) apply(bases[i]);
        else tryNext(i + 1);
      })
      .catch(function () { tryNext(i + 1); });
  }
  tryNext(0);
})();
</script>
```

## Start here

- [Install and run a first projection](01-getting-started.qmd)
- [Understand the input and output contract](02-inputs-and-outputs.qmd)
- [Work through a scenario](03-illustrative-example.qmd)
- [Use the API in an analysis workflow](04-workflow.qmd)
- [Understand the equation and its limitations](05-methodology.qmd)
- [Validate results against Excel](99-excel-parity-validation.qmd)

The public calculation surface is in `tiny_dsa.api`. The three functions
return labelled five-year series:

- `compute_output_baseline` calculates the baseline path.
- `compute_output_shocked` calculates the path after the selected shock.
- `compute_output_delta` returns shocked minus baseline, in percentage points
  of GDP.
